<description>
While looking into #36759 I discovered `-notorcontrol` did the opposite of what would be expected from it and I then checked for similar issues in other init options. There are several more where `-nofoo` does something surprising including one of them crashing the node.

This PR attempts to fix all these surprising behaviors while also keeping things as simple as possible and just change behavior to something that makes sense harmless in the context of the option. Fixes that use a common approach for the fix are grouped together into a commit even if the options included themselves may have no relation at all.

| Commit | Problematic options behavior | Fix approach |
|---|---|---|
| [mempool: Reject cluster limits below 1](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/512773d111daaa4330c873ed5889b9ef511f6e3a) | `-nolimitclustercount` hits an assertion in `TxGraph` on the first mempool transaction. `-nolimitclustersize` rejects every transaction. | Reject values below 1 at startup. |
| [args: Add NEGATE_TO_EMPTY so -nofoo reads as an empty string](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/ac4b8feb3fe151d1b00085cfe15a856ccede6e6e) | `GetArg()` returns `"0"` for a negated option. The `-no*notify` options run the command `0`, `-nosigner` uses `0` as signer, `-noi2psam` fails startup and `-norpcpassword` sets the password to `0`. Opt-in because options like `-noonion` and `-noblockfilterindex` depend on reading `"0"`. | New opt-in flag `NEGATE_TO_EMPTY` makes `GetArg()` return `""`. |
| [init: Read -cjdnsreachable and -help as booleans](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/dc4ddbacf791ac6742261bf66dcf42887bfb74ff) | `-cjdnsreachable=0` and `-nocjdnsreachable` turn CJDNS on. `-nohelp` prints the help. | Use `GetBoolArg()` instead of `IsArgSet()`. |
| [args, wallet: Fix empty and negated -blocksdir and -walletdir](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/be71581c2fc65722f6e335e6506cda342eb23ef7) | `-noblocksdir` writes block files relative to the working directory. `-nowalletdir` fails startup. | Fail at startup with `DISALLOW_NEGATION`. An empty value falls back to the default directory, like `-datadir` does. |
| [init: Require -nolistenonion with -notorcontrol](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/44b1c5b05057bf3a768eac63922c085163975dcc) | `-notorcontrol` connects to `0.0.0.0:9051`, which reaches a local Tor. | Fail at startup unless `-listenonion` is disabled. |
| [init: Disallow negating options where it has no meaning](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/6447b07919072f12aba36313814fd4962dd4363a) | `-nocheckblocks`, `-nomaxreceivebuffer`, `-nomaxsendbuffer` and `-nomaxtipage` read as 0, the opposite of what the user asked for. | Fail at startup with `DISALLOW_NEGATION`. |

`-nomempoolexpiry` has a similar kind of problem. It evicts transactions as soon as the next one arrives. I left it out because #36540 already is open and addresses this.
</description>

[2026-11-25] rc:4699787496 inline on src/wallet/init.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-25):
In commit "args: Add NEGATE_TO_EMPTY so -nofoo reads as an empty string" (fb15cb374f1a734ecf7dfcef11e56d8f082e9a4d)

The new `rpc_signer.py` check is failing in the "No wallet" CI job, and I think it found a real bug. In builds without the wallet, `-signer` is only registered by [`DummyWalletInit`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f65919e1159202e4bfe50f6b30f6493556ed0233/src/dummywallet.cpp#L42) as a plain hidden option, so it doesn't get `NEGATE_TO_EMPTY`, but the node still reads it, for example in the [`enumeratesigners`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f65919e1159202e4bfe50f6b30f6493556ed0233/src/rpc/external_signer.cpp#L49) RPC, so `-nosigner` still runs the command `0` there.

Since the node reads `-signer` whether or not the wallet is enabled, I think it should be registered as a node option instead of a wallet option. Moving this registration into `SetupServerArgs()` in `init.cpp`, inside the same `#ifdef ENABLE_EXTERNAL_SIGNER`, and dropping `-signer` from the `DummyWalletInit` list fixes the test for me in a no-wallet build. Keeping `OptionsCategory::WALLET` leaves the `-help` output unchanged in wallet builds.

(Not directly related to this PR, but it might be good for ArgsManager to handle placeholder options like the `DummyWalletInit` ones better. Currently they are registered as ordinary hidden options, the same way as real hidden options like `-dbcrashratio`, so setting them on the command line or in the config file is silently ignored, and nothing stops code from reading them. If they were marked as placeholders, ArgsManager could warn when they are set and raise an error when one is retrieved, which would have caught this bug even without a test.)
[2026-11-25] rc:4699787787 inline on test/functional/feature_notifications.py by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-25):
In commit "args: Add NEGATE_TO_EMPTY so -nofoo reads as an empty string" (fb15cb374f1a734ecf7dfcef11e56d8f082e9a4d)

The version of this test I posted in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36880#discussion_r4683423642 had a comment here saying the large-work invalid chain warning isn't raised again after node0 restarts, so `-alertnotify` couldn't be tested. That was wrong, and thanks for correcting it in this push: the warning is raised again, so the alert command would run without `-noalertnotify`. That means the "only checked for not running a bogus command" part no longer applies, and the test could check the alert file the same way as the other two options:

```python
        # node0 still has the large-work invalid chain from the test above, so
        # the warning is raised again on restart and -alertnotify would run.
        with open(self.alertnotify_file) as f:
            alert_text = f.read()
```

and after the `walletnotify` check:

```python
        with open(self.alertnotify_file) as f:
            assert_equal(f.read(), alert_text)
```

With that, the test fails if `-noalertnotify` is removed.

Thanks! It could also mention the settings that now work or mean something different, since those can change what a node does after upgrading too: `-blocksdir=` and `-walletdir=` now use the default directory, `-cjdnsreachable=0` and `-nocjdnsreachable` now disable CJDNS instead of enabling it, and negated options like `-norpcpassword`, `-nosigner` and `-noblocknotify` are now treated as empty instead of `0`, so `-norpcpassword` uses cookie authentication.
